## **6.3 Endowment and Reserves**

The institution's endowment fund, managed by Raiffeisen Capital Management AG under an investment mandate agreed in 2018 and most recently reviewed in October 2023, stood at €4,750,000 as of 31 December 2023, up from €4,480,000 at year-end 2022. The increase of €270,000 reflects investment returns of €161,800 (net of management fees) plus a transfer of €108,200 from the operating surplus pursuant to Board resolution KWM-BOARD-2023-12R02. The endowment mandate specifies a conservative to moderate risk profile with a target total return of 3.5–5.0% per annum and restrictions on equity exposure exceeding 30% of portfolio value. The Conservation Reserve Fund, established by Board resolution in 2019 and maintained as a designated reserve within the institution's accounts (not part of the endowment), received the full 2023 operating surplus of €367,160 and stood at €841,200 at year-end. This fund is designated exclusively for extraordinary conservation expenditure, defined in the reserve's governing policy as individual treatment projects exceeding €20,000 per work. Disbursements from this fund require Acquisitions Committee approval and Director General sign-off. KWM-DIR-2023-AR-001

## **1. Director General's Foreword**

The year 2023 marked a period of remarkable transformation and consolidation for Kunsthaus Wien. Under the continued stewardship of the Board of Trustees and with the tireless dedication of our 87 permanent staff members and 34 part-time associates, we achieved a record-breaking institutional performance that exceeded nearly every measurable target set in our 2021–2025 Strategic Plan. Our Director General, Dr. Maximilian Oberhuber-Steiner, assumed the post in January 2022 following the retirement of his predecessor, Dr. Eleonore Vásárhelyi, and has since led the institution through two major exhibition cycles, one significant acquisition campaign, and a complete overhaul of our digital infrastructure. This report covers the full fiscal year from 1 January to 31 December 2023 and represents the most comprehensive institutional selfassessment Kunsthaus Wien has produced in its thirty-one-year history. Among the highlights of 2023, we note the successful conclusion of the Secession Echoes retrospective in the spring, which attracted 28,412 visitors over its eleven-week run and became the most attended temporary exhibition in our institutional history. The autumn season brought the equally celebrated dual exhibition Farbe und Stille, co-organised with the Lentos Kunstmuseum Linz, which drew 19,847 visitors between September and November. Total annual footfall reached 94,620 visitors, surpassing the previous record of 88,340 set in 2019. From a financial perspective, the institution closed the year with total operating revenue of €6,284,500, against total expenditure of €5,917,340, yielding a modest but strategically meaningful surplus of €367,160. This surplus has been allocated in full to the Conservation Reserve Fund, consistent with the Board resolution of March 2023. The institution received public funding from the City of Vienna's Kulturabteilung (MA 7) in the amount of €2,100,000 and from the Austrian Federal Chancellery's Kunstsektion in the amount of €850,000, totalling €2,950,000 in public subsidy, which represented 46.9% of total operating revenue. We enter 2024 with cautious optimism. The global art market has shown signs of softening following exceptional growth in 2021 and 2022, and donor appetite for large-scale capital gifts has become more selective. Nevertheless, Kunsthaus Wien is well-positioned: our endowment stands at €4,750,000, our collection is insured at replacement value for €38,200,000, and our institutional partnerships span fourteen countries across Europe and the Americas. This document is intended solely for internal governance purposes and the use of the Board of Trustees, senior management, and approved statutory auditors."

## **6. Financial Report 2023**

## **9. Strategic Outlook and Risk Register**
## **9.1 Strategic Priorities for 2024–2025**

The final two years of the 2021–2025 Strategic Plan will be characterised by consolidation, evaluation, and preparation for the next planning cycle. Three strategic priorities have been identified by the Director General and endorsed by the Board at the December 2023 meeting. First, the institution will pursue a targeted acquisition campaign in the area of postwar Austrian women artists, for which the Acquisitions Committee has pre-approved a ring-fenced budget of €400,000 drawn from the Conservation Reserve Fund pending a formal Board resolution expected in March 2024. Dr. Riegler-Bauer has identified seven priority works across five artists whose estates or existing owners have expressed willingness to negotiate. The most significant target is a large-format triptych by Herta Kronauer-Weiß (1928–2004), currently in a private collection in Graz, which is estimated to be available for purchase at between €150,000 and €220,000. Second, the institution will undertake a full governance review in 2024, the first since 2017, to be conducted by external facilitator Dr. Monika Ehrenfeld-Strasser of Ehrenfeld Consulting (Vienna). The review will examine Board composition, trustee term limits, the delegation of authority matrix, and conflicts of interest policy. The engagement has been budgeted at €28,000 and will conclude with a written report to the Board no later than 30 September 2024. Third, and strategically most significant, the institution will formally launch a capital campaign in 2024 targeting a €2,000,000 increase in the endowment over a five-year horizon. The campaign will be led by a newly appointed Development Director, a role approved by the Board in October 2023 and currently in the final stages of recruitment. The shortlisted candidates are Mag. Florian Weidinger-Holub (currently Head of Development at the Vienna Philharmonic Foundation) and Dr. Brigitte Samuels-Baumann (currently Director of Philanthropy at the Kunsthistorisches Museum). ## **9.3 Note on Visitor Data Interpretation**

A note of caution is warranted regarding the interpretation of visitor statistics presented in Section 4. The total figure of 94,620 visitors represents gross recorded admissions and should not be used without adjustment for certain operational factors. Specifically, holders of the annual Kunsthaus Pass (of whom there were 1,847 active passholders as of 31 December 2023) are recorded as individual admissions on each visit, meaning frequent visitors may be counted multiple times within the annual total. Internal modelling by Mag. Zehetgruber's team suggests that adjusting for estimated repeat pass-holder visits would reduce the effective unique visitor count to approximately 81,200–83,400, though this estimate carries significant uncertainty. Furthermore, school groups are recorded at the point of guided tour commencement, not at point of ticket sale. In instances where a school group visits both the temporary and permanent exhibition spaces within a single visit, the group is counted once, not twice. This practice differs from the methodology used by some peer institutions, which count exhibition-level visits rather than person-level visits. Readers comparing KWM statistics to those of peer institutions should be aware of this methodological difference. ## **9.4 Correction to 2022 Annual Report**
